title: Cats vs Dogs: Who's Smarter, and Who Loves You More?
description:
Your cat knows its own name. It just doesn't come. And your dog grew a new face muscle just to work on you.

Cats vs dogs in 7 rounds, settled with real experiments, not opinions. Who moved in with humans first? Are dogs smarter than cats, and what happens when scientists count their brain cells? Do cats know their names? Dog nose vs cat ears. How do cats and dogs drink water (it's the same physics trick)? Puppy eyes vs the cat's purr. And the last round: do cats love their owners as much as dogs do?

Sources

• Jardim-Messeder, Herculano-Houzel et al., "Dogs have the most neurons, though not the largest brain", Frontiers in Neuroanatomy (2017)
• Pilley & Reid, Behavioural Processes (2011); Saito et al., "Domestic cats discriminate their names from other words", Scientific Reports (2019)
• Heffner, Behavioral Neuroscience (1983); Heffner & Heffner, "Hearing range of the domestic cat", Hearing Research (1985)
• Reis, Jung, Aristoff & Stocker, "How cats lap", Science (2010); Gart, Socha, Vlachos & Jung, "Dogs lap using acceleration-driven open pumping", PNAS (2015)
• Kaminski et al., "Evolution of facial muscle anatomy in dogs", PNAS (2019); Waller et al., PLOS ONE (2013)
• McComb et al., "The cry embedded within the purr", Current Biology (2009)
• Topál et al., J. Comparative Psychology (1998); Vitale, Behnke & Udell, "Attachment bonds between domestic cats and humans", Current Biology (2019)
• Every claim checked against 2+ sources. The round points are our own playful scoring.
